-Goal-
Given a text document that is potentially relevant to this activity and a list of entity types, identify all entities of those types from the text and all relationships among the identified entities.
 
-Steps-
1. Identify all entities. For each identified entity, extract the following information:
- entity_name: Name of the entity, capitalized
- entity_type: One of the following types: [organization,person,geo,event]
- entity_description: Comprehensive description of the entity's attributes and activities
Format each entity as ("entity"<|><entity_name><|><entity_type><|><entity_description>)
 
2. From the entities identified in step 1, identify all pairs of (source_entity, target_entity) that are *clearly related* to each other.
For each pair of related entities, extract the following information:
- source_entity: name of the source entity, as identified in step 1
- target_entity: name of the target entity, as identified in step 1
- relationship_description: explanation as to why you think the source entity and the target entity are related to each other
- relationship_strength: a numeric score indicating strength of the relationship between the source entity and target entity
 Format each relationship as ("relationship"<|><source_entity><|><target_entity><|><relationship_description><|><relationship_strength>)
 
3. Return output in English as a single list of all the entities and relationships identified in steps 1 and 2. Use **##** as the list delimiter.
 
4. When finished, output <|COMPLETE|>
 
######################
-Examples-
######################

Text: ataxia, cefaleas, epilepsia o trastornos ansioso-depresivos que se han querido relacionar con una posible hipoperfusión cerebral evidenciada en estos pacientes.

### 2.2.2. Artritis

Puede aparecer en el 26% de las formas de presentación en adultos y se sospecha su relación con la EC, ya que la eliminación del gluten de la dieta produce una clara disminución en su riesgo de aparición.

### 2.2.3. Hipoesplenismo

Se han descrito casos asociados a EC, con infecciones neumocócicas severas, por lo que se ha sugerido la necesidad de la vacunación profiláctica antineumocócica11. La etiopatogenia no se conoce.

### 2.2.4. Riesgo de aparición de neoplasias

Aunque no está suficientemente aclarado si existe un mayor riesgo de aparición de neoplasias de forma global12, sí parece estar aumentado el riesgo de aparición de ciertos tumores como linfoma intestinal no-Hodgkin y otros tumores gastroentéricos (esófago, intestino y colon). Por otro lado, también se ha referido un descenso en el riesgo de otras neoplasias, como de mama y probablemente pulmón.

## 2.3. Enfermedades asociadas

### 2.3.1. Dermatitis herpetiforme

Enfermedad cutánea vesículo-papulosa y pruriginosa de predominio en tronco y extremidades frecuentemente asociada a EC (24%). Su predisposición genética HLA-dependiente es común a la celiaquía y, como esta, mejora al eliminar el gluten de la dieta. Prácticamente la totalidad de los pacientes diagnosticados de dermatitis herpetiforme tienen lesiones parcheadas en la mucosa yeyunal, aunque asintomáticas en su mayor parte.

### 2.3.2. Diabetes mellitus tipo 1 (DM1)

Existe una prevalencia del 2,6-7,8% de anticuerpos antigliadina y antiendomisio en pacientes con DM1 adultos, y en muchos de estos se pueden demostrar lesiones en el intestino, aunque no presentan síntomas de la enfermedad. En niños diabéticos se ha reportado al menos un 3% de prevalencia de celiaquía. No está suficientemente aclarado la influencia de la EC sobre la DM1, ya que algunas evidencias de experimentación animal han referido un descenso en tasa de aparición y un retardo en la misma en animales predispuestos genéticamente a DM1 cuando se realiza dieta exenta en gluten. Esto no se ha podido demostrar en humanos. Sí parece claro que la regulación dietética del tratamiento de la celiaquía produce una mejoría en el control metabólico de la diabetes y en otros factores asociados13.

### 2.3.3. Déficit selectivo de IgA

Este aparece en el 1-2% de los pacientes celiacos.

### 2.3.4. Síndrome de Down

Existe un riesgo 100 veces mayor de aparición de celiaquía que en la población general, siendo la prevalencia de la biopsia intestinal positiva para celiaquía mayor del 16%.

### 2.3.5. Enfermedad hepática

Existe frecuentemente, desde elevaciones crónicas e inespecíficas de las enzimas hepáticas, hasta cuadros agudos de hepatitis autoinmune. Parece existir alguna relación también con la cirrosis biliar primaria, auque esta no ha sido confirmada en todos los estudios14.

### 2.3.6. Enfermedad tiroidea

Existe un aumento de la incidencia de trastornos tiroideos autoinmunes (6-8%) en los pacientes con celiaquía, siendo más frecuente la presencia de hipotiroidismo.

### 2.3.7. Trastornos ginecológico-obstétricos

Las pacientes celiacas sin tratamiento pueden tener retraso de menarquia, alteraciones menstruales y menopausia precoz. Esto asocia un cierto grado de infertilidad y mayor riesgo de gestaciones con retraso de crecimiento intrauterino. El tratamiento nutricional parece prevenir todos estos trastornos que probablemente se asocien a la malnutrición y los déficits vitamínicos asociados.

### 2.3.8. Miocarditis y miocardiopatía dilatada

No es muy frecuente la asociación, aunque en algunos estudios se ha encontrado EC hasta en un 5% de forma asintomática; en estos casos, la función cardiaca mejora al someterlo a dieta libre de gluten.

Given a text document that is potentially relevant to this activity and a list of entity types, identify all entities of those types from the text and all relationships among the identified entities.
 
-Steps-
1. Identify all entities. For each identified entity, extract the following information:
- entity_name: Name of the entity, capitalized
- entity_type: One of the following types: [organization,person,geo,event]
- entity_description: Comprehensive description of the entity's attributes and activities
Format each entity as ("entity"<|><entity_name><|><entity_type><|><entity_description>)
 
2. From the entities identified in step 1, identify all pairs of (source_entity, target_entity) that are *clearly related* to each other.

- source_entity: name of the source entity, as identified in step 1

You are an AI assistant that helps a human analyst to perform general information discovery. Information discovery is the process of identifying and assessing relevant information associated with certain entities (e.g., organizations and individuals) within a network.

# Goal
Write a comprehensive report of a community, given a list of entities that belong to the community as well as their relationships and optional associated claims. The report will be used to inform decision-makers about information associated with the community and their potential impact. The content of this report includes an overview of the community's key entities, their legal compliance, technical capabilities, reputation, and noteworthy claims.

# Report Structure

The report should include the following sections:

- TITLE: community's name that represents its key entities - title should be short but specific. When possible, include representative named entities in the title.
- SUMMARY: An executive summary of the community's overall structure, how its entities are related to each other, and significant information associated with its entities.
- IMPACT SEVERITY RATING: a float score between 0-10 that represents the severity of IMPACT posed by entities within the community.  IMPACT is the scored importance of a community.
- RATING EXPLANATION: Give a single sentence explanation of the IMPACT severity rating.
- DETAILED FINDINGS: A list of 5-10 key insights about the community. Each insight should have a short summary followed by multiple paragraphs of explanatory text grounded according to the grounding rules below. Be comprehensive.

Return output as a well-formed JSON-formatted string with the following format:
    {{
        "title": <report_title>,
        "summary": <executive_summary>,
        "rating": <impact_severity_rating>,
        "rating_explanation": <rating_explanation>,
        "findings": [
            {{
                "summary":<insight_1_summary>,
                "explanation": <insight_1_explanation>
            }},
            {{
                "summary":<insight_2_summary>,
                "explanation": <insight_2_explanation>
            }}
        ]
    }}

# Grounding Rules

Points supported by data should list their data references as follows:

"This is an example sentence supported by multiple data references [Data: <dataset name> (record ids); <dataset name> (record ids)]."

Do not list more than 5 record ids in a single reference. Instead, list the top 5 most relevant record ids and add "+more" to indicate that there are more.

For example:
"Person X is the owner of Company Y and subject to many allegations of wrongdoing [Data: Reports (1), Entities (5, 7); Relationships (23); Claims (7, 2, 34, 64, 46, +more)]."

where 1, 5, 7, 23, 2, 34, 46, and 64 represent the id (not the index) of the relevant data record.

Do not include information where the supporting evidence for it is not provided.

Write a comprehensive report of a community, given a list of entities that belong to the community as well as their relationships and optional associated claims. The report will be used to inform decision-makers about information associated with the community and their potential impact. The content of this report includes an overview of the community's key entities, their legal compliance, technical capabilities, reputation, and noteworthy claims.

The report should include the following sections:

- TITLE: community's name that represents its key entities - title should be short but specific. When possible, include representative named entities in the title.

Write a comprehensive report of a community, given a list of entities that belong to the community as well as their relationships and optional associated claims. The content of this report includes an overview of the community's key entities, their legal compliance, technical capabilities, reputation, and noteworthy claims.

You are an AI assistant that helps a human analyst to perform general information discovery. Information discovery is the process of identifying and assessing relevant information associated with certain entities (e.g., organizations and individuals) within a network.

# Goal
Write a comprehensive report of a community, given a list of entities that belong to the community as well as their relationships and optional associated claims. The report will be used to inform decision-makers about information associated with the community and their potential impact. The content of this report includes an overview of the community's key entities, their legal compliance, technical capabilities, reputation, and noteworthy claims.

# Report Structure

The report should include the following sections:

- TITLE: community's name that represents its key entities - title should be short but specific. When possible, include representative named entities in the title.
- SUMMARY: An executive summary of the community's overall structure, how its entities are related to each other, and significant information associated with its entities.
- IMPACT SEVERITY RATING: a float score between 0-10 that represents the severity of IMPACT posed by entities within the community.  IMPACT is the scored importance of a community.
- RATING EXPLANATION: Give a single sentence explanation of the IMPACT severity rating.
- DETAILED FINDINGS: A list of 5-10 key insights about the community. Each insight should have a short summary followed by multiple paragraphs of explanatory text grounded according to the grounding rules below. Be comprehensive.

Return output as a well-formed JSON-formatted string with the following format:
    {{
        "title": <report_title>,
        "summary": <executive_summary>,
        "rating": <impact_severity_rating>,
        "rating_explanation": <rating_explanation>,
        "findings": [
            {{
                "summary":<insight_1_summary>,
                "explanation": <insight_1_explanation>
            }},
            {{
                "summary":<insight_2_summary>,
                "explanation": <insight_2_explanation>
            }}
        ]
    }}

# Grounding Rules

Points supported by data should list their data references as follows:

"This is an example sentence supported by multiple data references [Data: <dataset name> (record ids); <dataset name> (record ids)]."

Do not list more than 5 record ids in a single reference. Instead, list the top 5 most relevant record ids and add "+more" to indicate that there are more.

For example:
"Person X is the owner of Company Y and subject to many allegations of wrongdoing [Data: Reports (1), Entities (5, 7); Relationships (23); Claims (7, 2, 34, 64, 46, +more)]."

where 1, 5, 7, 23, 2, 34, 46, and 64 represent the id (not the index) of the relevant data record.

You are an AI assistant that helps a human analyst to perform general information discovery. Information discovery is the process of identifying and assessing relevant information associated with certain entities (e.g., organizations and individuals) within a network.

# Goal
Write a comprehensive report of a community, given a list of entities that belong to the community as well as their relationships and optional associated claims. The report will be used to inform decision-makers about information associated with the community and their potential impact. The content of this report includes an overview of the community's key entities, their legal compliance, technical capabilities, reputation, and noteworthy claims.

You are an AI assistant that helps a human analyst to perform general information discovery. Information discovery is the process of identifying and assessing relevant information associated with certain entities (e.g., organizations and individuals) within a network.

# Goal
Write a comprehensive report of a community, given a list of entities that belong to the community as well as their relationships and optional associated claims. The report will be used to inform decision-makers about information associated with the community and their potential impact. The content of this report includes an overview of the community's key entities, their legal compliance, technical capabilities, reputation, and noteworthy claims.

# Report Structure

The report should include the following sections:

- TITLE: community's name that represents its key entities - title should be short but specific. When possible, include representative named entities in the title.
- SUMMARY: An executive summary of the community's overall structure, how its entities are related to each other, and significant information associated with its entities.
- IMPACT SEVERITY RATING: a float score between 0-10 that represents the severity of IMPACT posed by entities within the community.  IMPACT is the scored importance of a community.
- RATING EXPLANATION: Give a single sentence explanation of the IMPACT severity rating.
- DETAILED FINDINGS: A list of 5-10 key insights about the community. Each insight should have a short summary followed by multiple paragraphs of explanatory text grounded according to the grounding rules below. Be comprehensive.

Return output as a well-formed JSON-formatted string with the following format:
    {{
        "title": <report_title>,
        "summary": <executive_summary>,
        "rating": <impact_severity_rating>,
        "rating_explanation": <rating_explanation>,
        "findings": [
            {{
                "summary":<insight_1_summary>,
                "explanation": <insight_1_explanation>
            }},
            {{
                "summary":<insight_2_summary>,
                "explanation": <insight_2_explanation>
            }}
        ]
    }}

# Grounding Rules

Points supported by data should list their data references as follows:

"This is an example sentence supported by multiple data references [Data: <dataset name> (record ids); <dataset name> (record ids)]."

Do not list more than 5 record ids in a single reference. Instead, list the top 5 most relevant record ids and add "+more" to indicate that there are more.

For example:
"Person X is the owner of Company Y and subject to many allegations of wrongdoing [Data: Reports (1), Entities (5, 7); Relationships (23); Claims (7, 2, 34, 64, 46, +more)]."

where 1, 5, 7, 23, 2, 34, 46, and 64 represent the id (not the index) of the relevant data record.

Do not include information where the supporting evidence for it is not provided.

You are an AI assistant that helps a human analyst to perform general information discovery. Information discovery is the process of identifying and assessing relevant information associated with certain entities (e.g., organizations and individuals) within a network.

# Goal
Write a comprehensive report of a community, given a list of entities that belong to the community as well as their relationships and optional associated claims. The report will be used to inform decision-makers about information associated with the community and their potential impact. The content of this report includes an overview of the community's key entities, their legal compliance, technical capabilities, reputation, and noteworthy claims.

# Report Structure

The report should include the following sections:

- TITLE: community's name that represents its key entities - title should be short but specific. When possible, include representative named entities in the title.
- SUMMARY: An executive summary of the community's overall structure, how its entities are related to each other, and significant information associated with its entities.
- IMPACT SEVERITY RATING: a float score between 0-10 that represents the severity of IMPACT posed by entities within the community.  IMPACT is the scored importance of a community.
- RATING EXPLANATION: Give a single sentence explanation of the IMPACT severity rating.
- DETAILED FINDINGS: A list of 5-10 key insights about the community. Each insight should have a short summary followed by multiple paragraphs of explanatory text grounded according to the grounding rules below. Be comprehensive.

Return output as a well-formed JSON-formatted string with the following format:
    {{
        "title": <report_title>,
        "summary": <executive_summary>,
        "rating": <impact_severity_rating>,
        "rating_explanation": <rating_explanation>,
        "findings": [
            {{

            }},
            {{
                "summary":<insight_2_summary>,
                "explanation": <insight_2_explanation>
            }}
        ]
    }}

# Grounding Rules

Points supported by data should list their data references as follows:

"This is an example sentence supported by multiple data references [Data: <dataset name> (record ids); <dataset name> (record ids)]."

Do not list more than 5 record ids in a single reference. Instead, list the top 5 most relevant record ids and add "+more" to indicate that there are more.

For example:
"Person X is the owner of Company Y and subject to many allegations of wrongdoing [Data: Reports (1), Entities (5, 7); Relationships (23); Claims (7, 2, 34, 64, 46, +more)]."

where 1, 5, 7, 23, 2, 34, 46, and 64 represent the id (not the index) of the relevant data record.

Do not include information where the supporting evidence for it is not provided.

You are an AI assistant that helps a human analyst to perform general information discovery. Information discovery is the process of identifying and assessing relevant information associated with certain entities (e.g., organizations and individuals) within a network.

# Goal
Write a comprehensive report of a community, given a list of entities that belong to the community as well as their relationships and optional associated claims. The report will be used to inform decision-makers about information associated with the community and their potential impact. The content of this report includes an overview of the community's key entities, their legal compliance, technical capabilities, reputation, and noteworthy claims.

# Report Structure

The report should include the following sections:

- TITLE: community's name that represents its key entities - title should be short but specific. When possible, include representative named entities in the title.
- SUMMARY: An executive summary of the community's overall structure, how its entities are related to each other, and significant information associated with its entities.
- IMPACT SEVERITY RATING: a float score between 0-10 that represents the severity of IMPACT posed by entities within the community.  IMPACT is the scored importance of a community.
- RATING EXPLANATION: Give a single sentence explanation of the IMPACT severity rating.
- DETAILED FINDINGS: A list of 5-10 key insights about the community. Each insight should have a short summary followed by multiple paragraphs of explanatory text grounded according to the grounding rules below. Be comprehensive.

Return output as a well-formed JSON-formatted string with the following format:
    {{
        "title": <report_title>,
        "summary": <executive_summary>,
        "rating": <impact_severity_rating>,
        "rating_explanation": <rating_explanation>,
        "findings": [
            {{
                "summary":<insight_1_summary>,
                "explanation": <insight_1_explanation>
            }},
            {{
                "summary":<insight_2_summary>,
                "explanation": <insight_2_explanation>
            }}
        ]
    }}

# Grounding Rules

Points supported by data should list their data references as follows:

"This is an example sentence supported by multiple data references [Data: <dataset name> (record ids); <dataset name> (record ids)]."

Do not list more than 5 record ids in a single reference. Instead, list the top 5 most relevant record ids and add "+more" to indicate that there are more.

For example:
"Person X is the owner of Company Y and subject to many allegations of wrongdoing [Data: Reports (1), Entities (5, 7); Relationships (23); Claims (7, 2, 34, 64, 46, +more)]."

where 1, 5, 7, 23, 2, 34, 46, and 64 represent the id (not the index) of the relevant data record.

Do not include information where the supporting evidence for it is not provided.

# Goal
Write a comprehensive report of a community, given a list of entities that belong to the community as well as their relationships and optional associated claims. The report will be used to inform decision-makers about information associated with the community and their potential impact. The content of this report includes an overview of the community's key entities, their legal compliance, technical capabilities, reputation, and noteworthy claims.

# Goal
Write a comprehensive report of a community, given a list of entities that belong to the community as well as their relationships and optional associated claims. # Goal
Write a comprehensive report of a community, given a list of entities that belong to the community as well as their relationships and optional associated claims. The report will be used to inform decision-makers about information associated with the community and their potential impact. The content of this report includes an overview of the community's key entities, their legal compliance, technical capabilities, reputation, and noteworthy claims.

You are an AI assistant that helps a human analyst to perform general information discovery. Information discovery is the process of identifying and assessing relevant information associated with certain entities (e.g., organizations and individuals) within a network.

# Goal
Write a comprehensive report of a community, given a list of entities that belong to the community as well as their relationships and optional associated claims. The report will be used to inform decision-makers about information associated with the community and their potential impact. The content of this report includes an overview of the community's key entities, their legal compliance, technical capabilities, reputation, and noteworthy claims.

# Report Structure

The report should include the following sections:

- TITLE: community's name that represents its key entities - title should be short but specific. When possible, include representative named entities in the title.
- SUMMARY: An executive summary of the community's overall structure, how its entities are related to each other, and significant information associated with its entities.
- IMPACT SEVERITY RATING: a float score between 0-10 that represents the severity of IMPACT posed by entities within the community.  IMPACT is the scored importance of a community.
- RATING EXPLANATION: Give a single sentence explanation of the IMPACT severity rating.
- DETAILED FINDINGS: A list of 5-10 key insights about the community. Each insight should have a short summary followed by multiple paragraphs of explanatory text grounded according to the grounding rules below. Be comprehensive.

Return output as a well-formed JSON-formatted string with the following format:
    {{
        "title": <report_title>,
        "summary": <executive_summary>,
        "rating": <impact_severity_rating>,
        "rating_explanation": <rating_explanation>,
        "findings": [
            {{
                "summary":<insight_1_summary>,

            }},
            {{
                "summary":<insight_2_summary>,
                "explanation": <insight_2_explanation>
            }}
        ]

# Grounding Rules

Points supported by data should list their data references as follows:

"This is an example sentence supported by multiple data references [Data: <dataset name> (record ids); <dataset name> (record ids)]."

Do not list more than 5 record ids in a single reference. Instead, list the top 5 most relevant record ids and add "+more" to indicate that there are more.

For example:
"Person X is the owner of Company Y and subject to many allegations of wrongdoing [Data: Reports (1), Entities (5, 7); Relationships (23); Claims (7, 2, 34, 64, 46, +more)]."

where 1, 5, 7, 23, 2, 34, 46, and 64 represent the id (not the index) of the relevant data record.

367,"# Liver Health and Transplantation Community

The community focuses on various liver-related medical conditions, including hepatitis, liver cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma, along with their treatment options such as liver transplantation. The entities are interconnected through their relationships, highlighting the importance of nutritional support and the implications of muscle depletion in liver disease management.

## Hepatitis as a precursor to liver cirrhosis

Hepatitis is a significant medical condition that can lead to liver cirrhosis due to chronic inflammation and damage to liver cells. This relationship underscores the importance of early detection and management of hepatitis to prevent the progression to cirrhosis, which is a more severe and irreversible condition. Hepatitis can also manifest as a rare complication in patients undergoing ketogenic diet treatment, indicating the need for careful dietary management in affected individuals [Data: Entities (6708, 10220); Relationships (16011, 4957)].

You are an AI assistant that helps a human analyst to perform general information discovery. Information discovery is the process of identifying and assessing relevant information associated with certain entities (e.g., organizations and individuals) within a network.

# Goal
Write a comprehensive report of a community, given a list of entities that belong to the community as well as their relationships and optional associated claims. The report will be used to inform decision-makers about information associated with the community and their potential impact. The content of this report includes an overview of the community's key entities, their legal compliance, technical capabilities, reputation, and noteworthy claims.

# Report Structure

The report should include the following sections:

- TITLE: community's name that represents its key entities - title should be short but specific. When possible, include representative named entities in the title.
- SUMMARY: An executive summary of the community's overall structure, how its entities are related to each other, and significant information associated with its entities.
- IMPACT SEVERITY RATING: a float score between 0-10 that represents the severity of IMPACT posed by entities within the community.  IMPACT is the scored importance of a community.
- RATING EXPLANATION: Give a single sentence explanation of the IMPACT severity rating.
- DETAILED FINDINGS: A list of 5-10 key insights about the community. Each insight should have a short summary followed by multiple paragraphs of explanatory text grounded according to the grounding rules below. Be comprehensive.

Return output as a well-formed JSON-formatted string with the following format:
    {{
        "title": <report_title>,
        "summary": <executive_summary>,
        "rating": <impact_severity_rating>,
        "rating_explanation": <rating_explanation>,
        "findings": [
            {{
                "summary":<insight_1_summary>,
                "explanation": <insight_1_explanation>
            }},
            {{
                "summary":<insight_2_summary>,
                "explanation": <insight_2_explanation>
            }}
        ]
    }}

# Grounding Rules

Points supported by data should list their data references as follows:

"This is an example sentence supported by multiple data references [Data: <dataset name> (record ids); <dataset name> (record ids)]."

Do not list more than 5 record ids in a single reference. Instead, list the top 5 most relevant record ids and add "+more" to indicate that there are more.

For example:
"Person X is the owner of Company Y and subject to many allegations of wrongdoing [Data: Reports (1), Entities (5, 7); Relationships (23); Claims (7, 2, 34, 64, 46, +more)]."

where 1, 5, 7, 23, 2, 34, 46, and 64 represent the id (not the index) of the relevant data record.

Do not include information where the supporting evidence for it is not provided.

372,"# Nutritional Management in Healthcare

The community focuses on the interrelated entities involved in nutritional management within healthcare settings, particularly emphasizing the role of ALIMENTOS in patient care, dietary adaptations, and food safety. Key entities include hospital caterers, dietary guidelines, and specific medical conditions that influence food intake and preparation.

## ALIMENTOS as a cornerstone of clinical nutrition

ALIMENTOS represents a broad category of food products essential for clinical nutrition, particularly in managing specific dietary needs and health outcomes. These food items are formulated to meet various nutritional requirements and are subject to safety regulations to prevent contamination. The significance of ALIMENTOS is underscored by its role in supporting patients with diverse health conditions, including those requiring modified diets due to dysphagia or other medical issues. Proper management of ALIMENTOS is crucial for ensuring patient safety and promoting recovery. [Data: Entities (552); Relationships (527, 295, 3840)]

## The relationship between ALIMENTOS and hyperfosfatemia

HYPERFOSFATEMIA is a medical condition that can arise from excessive intake of phosphate-rich foods, making the management of ALIMENTOS particularly important for patients with renal issues. Dietary adjustments are often necessary to control phosphate levels effectively, highlighting the need for careful monitoring of food intake in affected patients. This relationship emphasizes the critical role of dietary management in preventing complications associated with hyperfosfatemia. [Data: Entities (11523); Relationships (3512, 3864)]

## Cocina's role in patient meal preparation

Cocina refers to the kitchen facilities in hospitals, which are essential for preparing and serving meals tailored to patients' dietary needs. The quality and safety of food prepared in the Cocina directly impact patient health outcomes, making it a vital component of healthcare nutrition. Ensuring that the Cocina adheres to food safety standards is crucial for preventing contamination and ensuring that patients receive safe and nutritious meals. [Data: Entities (8224); Relationships (1035, 3844)]

## Hospital Caterers' guidelines for dietary adaptations

Hospital Caterers is an organization that provides guidelines and resources for food services in hospitals, focusing on dietary adaptations for patients with specific needs, such as those with dysphagia. Their role is critical in ensuring that hospitals can meet the diverse dietary requirements of patients, thereby enhancing the quality of care and nutrition provided. This organization plays a significant role in shaping food service practices within healthcare settings. [Data: Entities (834); Relationships (2159)]

## The importance of APPCC in food safety

APPCC (Análisis de Peligros y Puntos de Control Crítico) is a comprehensive food safety management system that ensures hygiene and safety across food operations, particularly in sensitive environments like hospitals. By identifying and controlling potential hazards throughout the food production process, APPCC plays a vital role in safeguarding public health and ensuring the integrity of food products served to patients. This system is essential for maintaining high safety standards in hospital kitchens. [Data: Entities (836); Relationships (5112, 5113)]

## Nutritional interactions with medications

The interaction between ALIMENTOS and medications is significant, as certain foods can affect the absorption and efficacy of drugs like Paracetamol and Amoxicillin. Understanding these interactions is crucial for optimizing patient care, particularly for those on complex medication regimens. This highlights the importance of dietary education and tailored nutritional guidance in managing patients' overall health and treatment outcomes. [Data: Entities (14202, 14201); Relationships (3873, 3872)]"
371,"# Food Allergies and Related Conditions

The community focuses on food allergies and their associated conditions, including various immune responses and gastrointestinal issues. Key entities such as food allergies, mucosal integrity, and specific allergic reactions are interconnected, highlighting the complexity of managing these health concerns.

## Food allergies as a critical health issue

Food allergies represent a significant public health concern, characterized by adverse immune responses to specific food items. These allergies can lead to severe reactions, including anaphylaxis, which can be life-threatening. The prevalence of food allergies has been increasing, necessitating greater awareness and management strategies. The relationship between food allergies and various conditions such as urticaria, anaphylaxis, and gastrointestinal disorders underscores the complexity of this issue [Data: Entities (14000, 14002, 14003); Relationships (19717, 19718, 19722, 19733, 19734)].

## The role of mucosal integrity in food allergies

The integrity of the intestinal mucosa is crucial in preventing food allergies. A compromised mucosal barrier can allow the passage of allergens, triggering immune responses that lead to allergic reactions. Maintaining mucosal health through proper nutrition is essential for individuals at risk of developing food allergies. This relationship highlights the importance of enteral nutrition in reducing the risk of allergic reactions [Data: Entities (2150, 14000); Relationships (9004, 19724)].

## Diverse allergic reactions linked to food allergies

Food allergies can manifest in various forms, including urticaria, angioedema, and gastrointestinal symptoms. Each of these reactions involves different immune mechanisms and can significantly impact the quality of life for affected individuals. Understanding the spectrum of allergic reactions is vital for effective diagnosis and management, as different reactions may require distinct treatment approaches [Data: Entities (14002, 14006, 14007); Relationships (19717, 19721, 19722)].

## The significance of IgE in food allergies

Immunoglobulin E (IgE) plays a central role in the pathophysiology of food allergies, mediating the immune response to allergens. Elevated IgE levels are often associated with severe allergic reactions, making it a critical biomarker for diagnosis and management. Understanding the mechanisms of IgE production and its role in allergic responses is essential for developing targeted therapies [Data: Entities (14013, 14000); Relationships (19724, 19726)].

## Cross-reactivity and oral allergy syndrome

Oral allergy syndrome is a condition where individuals with certain food allergies experience allergic reactions to proteins in fruits and vegetables that cross-react with pollen allergens. This phenomenon complicates the management of food allergies and highlights the need for comprehensive allergy testing and patient education to avoid potential triggers [Data: Entities (14031, 14000); Relationships (19732)].

## The impact of bacterial toxins on food allergies

Bacterial toxins can provoke adverse reactions similar to those seen in food allergies, complicating the clinical picture for affected individuals. Understanding the role of these toxins in allergic responses is crucial for developing effective management strategies and preventing allergic reactions triggered by contaminated food [Data: Entities (14008, 14000); Relationships (19723)].

## The role of research organizations in food allergy management

Organizations such as Fundación BBVA and SEAIC are pivotal in advancing the understanding and management of food allergies. Their research contributes to the development of guidelines and educational resources that help healthcare providers and patients navigate the complexities of food allergies, ultimately improving patient outcomes [Data: Entities (14096, 14097); Relationships (19743, 19744)]."
373,"# Allergies and Symptoms Community

The community focuses on the interrelated entities concerning allergies, food intolerances, and their associated symptoms. Key entities include Síntomas, Alergias e Intolerancias Alimentarias, and AEPNAA, which collectively address the diagnosis, treatment, and management of allergic reactions and related health issues.

## Síntomas as a central entity

Síntomas plays a crucial role in the community as it encompasses a wide range of clinical manifestations associated with various medical conditions, particularly allergies and intolerances. Symptoms are vital for diagnosing conditions like diabetes, malnutrition, and chronic pancreatitis, highlighting their importance in clinical assessments. For instance, symptoms such as increased thirst and frequent urination are key indicators of diabetes, while abdominal pain and weight loss are significant in chronic pancreatitis. The diverse nature of symptoms across different conditions underscores the need for careful monitoring and management in affected patients [Data: Entities (505); Relationships (3647, 3653, 3651, 3652, 3654, +more)].

## Alergias e Intolerancias Alimentarias as a comprehensive resource

The entity Alergias e Intolerancias Alimentarias provides a comprehensive overview of food allergies and intolerances, including their diagnosis and treatment. This entity discusses mechanisms of tolerance and desensitization, as well as the symptoms associated with these conditions. It also covers various diagnostic tests, such as the prick test and RAST, which are essential for identifying food allergies. The focus on diagnostic and treatment strategies makes this entity a critical resource for patients and healthcare providers alike [Data: Entities (14026); Relationships (3869, 13176, 19760, 19761, +more)].

## The role of AEPNAA in patient support

AEPNAA serves as an important organization dedicated to providing information and support for individuals dealing with allergies and food intolerances. It acts as a forum for sharing experiences and updates on food safety, which is crucial for patients who need to avoid allergens. The collaboration with other entities, such as Alergias e Intolerancias Alimentarias, enhances the community's ability to provide comprehensive support and resources for affected individuals [Data: Entities (14076); Relationships (19761, 19789, +more)].

## Importance of diagnostic tests in managing allergies

Diagnostic tests such as the prick test and RAST are essential tools in the identification and management of food allergies. These tests help determine the presence of specific IgE antibodies, which are critical for diagnosing allergic reactions. The relationship between these tests and the entity Alergias e Intolerancias Alimentarias emphasizes the importance of accurate diagnosis in developing effective treatment plans for patients [Data: Entities (14050, 14051); Relationships (19756, 19757, +more)].

## Symptoms linked to specific conditions

The symptoms associated with various conditions, such as classic galactosemia and dumping syndrome, illustrate the diverse manifestations of allergies and intolerances. For example, classic galactosemia presents symptoms like food rejection and vomiting, while dumping syndrome can lead to abdominal discomfort and nausea. Understanding these specific symptoms is crucial for timely diagnosis and intervention, which can significantly impact patient outcomes [Data: Entities (505, 5949); Relationships (3649, 3654, +more)]."
377,"# Allergic Gastrointestinal Disorders Community

This community encompasses various allergic gastrointestinal disorders, including esophagitis eosinophílica, celiac disease, and gastroenteritis eosinofílica. The entities are interconnected through their relationships with food allergies and their impact on gastrointestinal health, highlighting the complexity of diagnosis and treatment in this area.

## Esofagitis eosinofílica as a common cause of dysphagia

Esofagitis eosinofílica is frequently diagnosed in patients experiencing dysphagia, which is difficulty swallowing. This condition is characterized by eosinophilic infiltration in the esophagus, often linked to food allergies. The diagnosis typically involves endoscopy, which allows for direct visualization and biopsy of the esophageal tissue to confirm inflammation. The relationship between esofagitis eosinofílica and dysphagia underscores the importance of recognizing allergic conditions in patients presenting with swallowing difficulties [Data: Relationships (288)].

## Celiac disease and its nutritional implications

Celiac disease is an autoimmune disorder that leads to malabsorption of essential nutrients due to damage in the small intestine caused by gluten. This malabsorption can result in various health issues, including an increased risk of kidney stones and iron deficiency anemia. The complexity of celiac disease is highlighted by its differential diagnosis with other conditions, such as mitochondrial diseases and gastroenteritis eosinofílica, which can present similar symptoms. The need for a strict gluten-free diet is crucial for managing celiac disease and preventing long-term complications [Data: Entities (2572); Relationships (10196, 10195)].

## Gastroenteritis eosinofílica linked to food allergies

Gastroenteritis eosinofílica is an inflammatory condition of the gastrointestinal tract associated with food allergies. It can manifest at any age and is characterized by severe gastrointestinal symptoms, including vomiting and diarrhea. The diagnosis is confirmed through the presence of eosinophils in gastric or intestinal biopsies. The relationship between gastroenteritis eosinofílica and food allergies emphasizes the need for careful dietary management and allergy testing in affected individuals [Data: Entities (10515); Relationships (18315)].

## The role of food allergies in these conditions

Food allergies play a significant role in the development and exacerbation of conditions such as esofagitis eosinofílica, celiac disease, and gastroenteritis eosinofílica. These allergic reactions can lead to inflammation and damage in the gastrointestinal tract, necessitating a comprehensive approach to diagnosis and treatment. Understanding the interplay between these allergic conditions is essential for effective management and improving patient outcomes [Data: Entities (14037); Relationships (3667, 3668, 18316)].

## Importance of dietary interventions

Dietary interventions, such as elimination diets and oral provocations, are critical in diagnosing and managing food allergies. The elimination diet involves removing suspected allergens from the diet for a period, followed by reintroduction to confirm the allergy. This method is particularly relevant for conditions like esofagitis eosinofílica and gastroenteritis eosinofílica, where specific food proteins, such as those from soy and cow's milk, can trigger symptoms. The role of allergologists in guiding these dietary strategies is vital for effective management [Data: Entities (14054, 14055); Relationships (19769, 19770, 19771)]."
370,"# Dieta Hiposódica y Alimentos Relacionados

La comunidad se centra en las dietas hiposódicas, específicamente la dieta hiposódica estricta y moderada, y su relación con varios alimentos, como pistachos, almendras y ciruelas secas. Estas entidades están interconectadas a través de sus efectos en la salud y la gestión del sodio en la dieta.

## Importancia de la dieta hiposódica estricta

La dieta hiposódica estricta es fundamental para controlar la ingesta de sodio, especialmente en personas con condiciones de salud como la hiponatremia. Esta dieta incluye una selección específica de alimentos que ayudan a mantener niveles adecuados de sodio y potasio, lo que es crucial para la salud cardiovascular. La relación entre la dieta hiposódica estricta y la hiponatremia destaca la necesidad de un seguimiento cuidadoso de la ingesta de sodio y potasio [Data: Entities (11359); Relationships (7834, 3860, 8223)].

## Dieta hiposódica moderada y su relevancia

La dieta hiposódica moderada también juega un papel importante en la gestión de la ingesta de sodio, aunque con un enfoque menos restrictivo que la dieta estricta. Esta dieta permite una mayor variedad de alimentos, lo que puede facilitar la adherencia a largo plazo. Sin embargo, sigue siendo esencial evitar alimentos ricos en sodio para mantener la salud [Data: Entities (11358); Relationships (3859, 8222, 18700)].

## Pistachos como opción saludable

Los pistachos son un alimento recomendado en ambas dietas hiposódicas, gracias a su bajo contenido de sodio y sus beneficios para la salud cardiovascular. Se ha demostrado que su consumo está asociado con una reducción de la presión arterial, lo que los convierte en una opción ideal para quienes siguen una dieta hiposódica. Además, su valor nutricional, que incluye hierro y grasas saludables, los hace destacar en este contexto [Data: Entities (7315); Relationships (16423, 16422)].

## Alimentos a evitar en dietas hiposódicas

Los alimentos ricos en sodio son estrictamente desaconsejados en las dietas hiposódicas, ya que pueden contrarrestar los beneficios de estas dietas. La identificación y evitación de estos alimentos son cruciales para el éxito de cualquier plan de dieta hiposódica. Esto incluye una variedad de productos procesados y ciertos tipos de frutos secos que pueden tener un alto contenido de sodio [Data: Entities (11362); Relationships (18706, 18700)].

## Beneficios de las ciruelas secas y otros frutos secos

Las ciruelas secas, junto con otros frutos secos como almendras y avellanas, son recomendadas en las dietas hiposódicas por su bajo contenido de sodio y sus beneficios digestivos. Estos alimentos no solo ayudan a controlar la ingesta de sodio, sino que también aportan nutrientes esenciales que pueden mejorar la salud general. Su inclusión en la dieta hiposódica puede ser beneficiosa para quienes buscan opciones saludables y sabrosas [Data: Entities (10867, 11364, 11363); Relationships (18488, 18701)]."
380,"# Dysphagia Assessment Community

The Dysphagia Assessment Community is centered around various clinical methods and tools designed to evaluate swallowing disorders, particularly dysphagia. Key entities include the Método de Exploración Clínica Volumen-Viscosidad (MECV-V), bolus characteristics, and videoendoscopic exploration techniques, all of which are interconnected in assessing and treating swallowing difficulties.

## MECV-V as a primary assessment method

The Método de Exploración Clínica Volumen-Viscosidad (MECV-V) is a non-invasive clinical assessment method specifically designed to evaluate dysphagia. This method is crucial as it utilizes different food volumes and viscosities to assess swallowing safety and efficacy, making it a cornerstone in the evaluation of patients with swallowing difficulties. The MECV-V method is directly linked to dysphagia, as it is employed to assess and evaluate this condition in patients, highlighting its importance in clinical settings [Data: Entities (282); Relationships (358, 133, 2251, 2249)].

## Role of bolus in swallowing assessments

Bolus, defined as a mass of substance typically food or liquid, plays a critical role in the assessment of swallowing disorders. During evaluations, boluses of varying volumes and viscosities are administered to patients, allowing clinicians to observe and assess their swallowing capabilities. The relationship between bolus characteristics and the MECV-V method is significant, as the latter relies on these variations to provide a comprehensive evaluation of swallowing safety [Data: Entities (284); Relationships (2249, 2252, 2253)].

## Videoendoscopic exploration techniques

Videoendoscopic exploration is a vital procedure used to evaluate swallowing by observing anatomy and swallowing mechanics. This method is based on principles established by Dr. Langmore and is essential for diagnosing swallowing disorders. The integration of videoendoscopic exploration with tools like the videoendoscope and high-definition screens enhances the clarity and effectiveness of assessments, making it a key component in the community's approach to dysphagia [Data: Entities (400); Relationships (3025, 3029, 3030)].

## Dr. P. Clavé Civit's contributions

Dr. P. Clavé Civit is a pivotal figure in the Dysphagia Assessment Community, having designed the MECV-V method for assessing swallowing disorders. His contributions are foundational, as the MECV-V method is widely recognized and utilized in clinical practice. The relationship between Dr. Clavé and the MECV-V method underscores the importance of expert input in developing effective assessment tools for dysphagia [Data: Entities (281); Relationships (2248)].

## Importance of monitoring tools like pulse oximeters

The community focuses on various liver-related medical conditions, including hepatitis, liver cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma, along with their treatment options such as liver transplantation. ## Hepatitis as a precursor to liver cirrhosis

Hepatitis is a significant medical condition that can lead to liver cirrhosis due to chronic inflammation and damage to liver cells. This relationship underscores the importance of early detection and management of hepatitis to prevent the progression to cirrhosis, which is a more severe and irreversible condition. Hepatitis can also manifest as a rare complication in patients undergoing ketogenic diet treatment, indicating the need for careful dietary management in affected individuals [Data: Entities (6708, 10220); Relationships (16011, 4957)].

## Liver cirrhosis and its complications

Liver cirrhosis represents a late stage of liver disease characterized by the replacement of healthy liver tissue with scar tissue, significantly impairing liver function.
